_description:
Manual name corrections for CHANGES-UM dataset matching.
Each entry maps our waterbody name to the dataset lake name for a given county.
Format: county -> our_name -> dataset_name

Detroit River.source: Michigan DNR / USGS St. Clair–Detroit River System surveys

Au Sable River.source: Michigan DNR trout-stream classification / Michigan Fishing Guide
Au Sable River.note: DNR classifies the Au Sable River in Crawford County as a Class I (self-sustaining wild trout) trout stream with ~69.1 miles of classified trout water. Verified species list from https://michiganfishing.guide/trout-streams/au-sable-river-crawford/ (data sourced from Michigan DNR Division of Fish and Wildlife). Wikipedia and DNR Trout Trails also confirm brown, brook and rainbow trout in the system.

Manistee River.source: Michigan DNR Status of the Fishery Resource Report 2020-283 / Michigan DNR inland trout regulations
Manistee River.note: The Upper Manistee River flows through Crawford County (headwaters to Sharon, crossing Antrim/Otsego/Crawford/Kalkaska). DNR report 0345_2020_UpperManisteeRiver.pdf documents self-sustaining brook and brown trout populations and notes rainbow trout in tributaries; DNR trout regulations specifically regulate Brook, Brown and Rainbow Trout on the Manistee River (Crawford Co.) from Co. Rd. 612 to M-72 and from M-72 to CCC Bridge. Migratory salmon/steelhead are blocked by downstream dams and are not present in the Crawford County reach.

Flat River.source: Safe Harbor Fishing / Fishbrain / Fox17 DNR electrofishing coverage
Flat River.note: Safe Harbor Fishing lists bass, pike, walleye, panfish, catfish, bullhead, carp for the Flat River. Fishbrain catches and Fox17 DNR electrofishing confirm smallmouth. No dedicated DNR Status report found for the Flat River itself. URL: https://safeharborfishing.com/what-fish-are-in-the-flat-river

Pine River (Chippewa River tributary).source: Michigan DNR Status of the Fishery Resource Report 2015-201, Alma Impoundment
Pine River (Chippewa River tributary).note: DNR report documents Upper Pine River/Alma Impoundment species. This covers the downstream impoundment, same river system. URL: https://www2.dnr.state.mi.us/publications/pdfs/DNRFishLibrary/StatusoftheFisheryResourceReports/0268_2015_AlmaImpoundment.pdf

Black River.note: Fishbrain logged catches list Channel Catfish, Walleye, Smallmouth Bass, Largemouth Bass, Rock Bass, White Crappie and Bowfin. onWater cites a 2013 fisheries survey documenting Brook Trout, Rainbow Trout, Chinook Salmon and Coho Salmon, plus salmon spawning runs. Local sources also note Brown Trout, Lake Trout, Common Carp, Northern Pike, Yellow Perch and Whitefish. URLs: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/QqfXKnQf/black-river and https://www.onwaterapp.com/us/michigan/water/black-river-w7

Cass River.note: Cass River Water Trail states Rock bass, smallmouth bass, largemouth bass, bluegills, pumpkinseed sunfish, northern pike and catfish are very common; sturgeon and walleye are recovering species. Display names normalized to the angl3r species list. URL: https://cassriverwatertrail.org/explore/fishing

Mill Creek and Tributaries.source: Michigan DNR Trout Trails / Status of the Fishery Resource PDF TT2015087
Mill Creek and Tributaries.note: DNR Trout Trails PDF for Mill Creek Flaherty Park describes a Type 1 trout stream with stocked/wild Brown Trout, wild Steelhead (Rainbow Trout), and occasional Chinook/Coho Salmon moving in from the Paw Paw River. PDF: https://www.dnr.state.mi.us/publications/pdfs/ArcGISOnline/StoryMaps/fish_troutTrails/PDFs/TT2015087.pdf

Boyle Lake.source: Fishbrain (Berrien County, Michigan — named catch records)
Boyle Lake.note: Fishbrain lists top species as Largemouth Bass, Black Crappie, Bluegill; logged catches also include Yellow Perch and Redear Sunfish. URL: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/c93m5HwA/boyle-lake

Brush Lake.source: Fishbrain (Berrien County, Michigan — named catch records)
Brush Lake.note: Fishbrain lists top species as Bluegill and Largemouth Bass. URL: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/eGH7Zbt_/brush-lake

Colvin Lake.source: Fishbrain (Berrien County, Michigan — named catch records)
Colvin Lake.note: Fishbrain only reports Largemouth Bass as the most popular species for Colvin Lake; no additional survey data found. URL: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/YKXG95re/colvin-lake

Coveney Lake.source: Generalized southwest Michigan warmwater lake assemblage
Coveney Lake.note: No waterbody-specific species source (DNR report, stocking record, or named catch database) was found for Coveney Lake. Species list inferred from typical Berrien County small-lake fish communities.

Deer Creek.source: Generalized southwest Michigan warmwater creek assemblage
Deer Creek.note: No waterbody-specific species source was found for Deer Creek (South Branch Galien River tributary). Nearby South Branch Galien River supports trout, but Deer Creek itself is unverified.

Garwood Lake.source: Fishbrain (Berrien County, Michigan — named catch records)
Garwood Lake.note: Fishbrain lists top species as Largemouth Bass, Black Crappie, and Black Bullhead. URL: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/oZruaQS7/garwood-lake

Half Moon Lake.source: Generalized southwest Michigan warmwater lake assemblage
Half Moon Lake.note: No waterbody-specific species source was found for Half Moon Lake (Berrien County). Online sources for other Michigan Half Moon Lakes are not applicable to this Berrien County waterbody.

Harris Lake.source: Fishbrain (Berrien County, Michigan — named catch records)
Harris Lake.note: Fishbrain lists Bluegill as the only reported top species for Harris Lake. URL: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/sJtE58DU/harris-lake

Jarvis Lake.source: Fishbrain (Berrien County, Michigan — named catch records)
Jarvis Lake.note: Fishbrain lists top species as Largemouth Bass and Bluegill. URL: https://fishbrain.com/fishing-waters/CASruQ2D/jarvis-lake
